lines.en: HERE BEGINS THE EPISTLE OF MASHA'ALLAH

lines.text: LAE DE REBVS ECLIPSIVM, ET DE
lines.en: CONCERNING THE MATTERS OF ECLIPSES, AND CONCERNING
the conjunctions of the Planets, in the revolu-
tions of the years of the world, briefly eluci-
dated, and there are in it chapters
twelve.

lines.text: PRimum caput est de ratione circuli & stellarum, & qua-
lines.en: The first chapter is concerning the nature of the circle and of the stars, and how
they operate in this world.

lines.text: Secundum caput de diuersitate uestigij, hoc est, operis stella
lines.en: The second chapter concerning the diversity of the trace, that is, of the operation of the stars
in the regions of the earth.

lines.text: Tertium caput de signis eorum calidis scilicet & frigidis, &
lines.en: The third chapter concerning their signs, namely hot and cold, and

lines.text: quæ sint ex eis fixa uel mobilia, diurna aut nocturna.
lines.en: which of them are fixed or mobile, diurnal or nocturnal.

lines.text: Quartum caput de reuolutione annorum mundi.
lines.en: The fourth chapter concerning the revolution of the years of the world.

lines.text: Quintum caput de eclipsi Lunæ & eius significatione.
lines.en: The fifth chapter concerning the eclipse of the Moon and its signification.

lines.text: Sextum caput de mutatione temporum, per mutationem
lines.en: The sixth chapter concerning the mutation of times, through the mutation
of the planets in the signs of the heavy ones.

lines.text: Septimum caput de Eclipsi Solis & eius significatione.
lines.en: The seventh chapter concerning the Eclipse of the Sun and its signification.

lines.text: Octauum caput de coniunctione planetarũ, & eius opere.
lines.en: The eighth chapter concerning the conjunction of the planets, and its operation.
The ninth concerning the conjunction of the higher planets.
The tenth chapter concerning the major conjunction.
The eleventh concerning the mean conjunction.
The twelfth, concerning the minor conjunction.
CHAPTER I. CONCERNING THE NATURE OF THE CIRCLE,
and of the stars, and how they operate
in this world.

lines.text: SCito quòd dominus altissimus fecit terram ad similitudi-
lines.en: Know that the most high Lord made the earth in the likeness

lines.text: nem sphæræ, & fecit circulum altiorem in circuitu eiusdẽ
lines.en: of a sphere, and made a higher circle in the circuit of the same

lines.text: uolubilẽ, posuitq́; terram fixam & immobilem in medio cir-
lines.en: revolving, and placed the earth fixed and immobile in the middle of the cir-

summary.headline: Māshāʾallāh on Eclipses
summary.text: Māshāʾallāh’s epistle on eclipses and planetary conjunctions outlines twelve chapters on celestial circles, stars, regional stellar influences, planetary signs and motions, world-year revolutions, lunar and solar eclipses, mutations of times, and major, mean, minor, and superior-planet conjunctions. Chapter I begins with the nature of the circle and stars and their operation in the world.
